1→# Getting Started: Your First Plugin
     2→
     3→This tutorial walks you through creating, developing, testing, and publishing an OpenACP plugin from scratch. No prior knowledge of OpenACP internals is required.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Prerequisites
     8→
     9→- **Node.js** 18+ installed
    10→- **npm** or **pnpm** installed
    11→- **OpenACP** installed globally (`npm install -g @openacp/cli`)
    12→- A working OpenACP setup (run `openacp onboard` if you haven't yet)
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Step 1: Scaffold a New Plugin
    17→
    18→Run the scaffold command:
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→openacp plugin create
    22→```
    23→
    24→You will be prompted for:
    25→
    26→```
    27→◆  Create a new OpenACP plugin
    28→│
    29→◇  Plugin name (e.g., @myorg/adapter-matrix)
    30→│  @myorg/hello-world
    31→│
    32→◇  Description
    33→│  A greeting plugin for OpenACP
    34→│
    35→◇  Author
    36→│  Your Name <you@example.com>
    37→│
    38→◇  License
    39→│  MIT
    40→│
    41→◆  Plugin scaffolded!
    42→│
    43→│  Next steps
    44→│
    45→│  cd hello-world
    46→│  npm install
    47→│  npm run build
    48→│  npm test
    49→│
    50→│  # Start development with hot-reload:
    51→│  openacp dev .
    52→│
    53→└  Plugin @myorg/hello-world created in ./hello-world
    54→```
    55→
    56→The scaffold creates a directory named after your plugin (without the scope prefix):
    57→
    58→```
    59→hello-world/
    60→  src/
    61→    index.ts                  # Plugin entry point
    62→    __tests__/
    63→      index.test.ts           # Test file
    64→  package.json
    65→  tsconfig.json
    66→  .gitignore
    67→  .npmignore
    68→  .editorconfig
    69→  README.md
    70→```
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→## Step 2: Explore the Template
    75→
    76→### package.json
    77→
    78→Key fields in the generated `package.json`:
    79→
    80→```json
    81→{
    82→  "name": "@myorg/hello-world",
    83→  "version": "0.1.0",
    84→  "type": "module",
    85→  "main": "dist/index.js",
    86→  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
    87→  "scripts": {
    88→    "build": "tsc",
    89→    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    90→    "test": "vitest",
    91→    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build"
    92→  },
    93→  "peerDependencies": {
    94→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0"
    95→  },
    96→  "devDependencies": {
    97→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0",
    98→    "typescript": "^5.4.0",
    99→    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
   100→  }
   101→}
   102→```
   103→
   104→The `@openacp/plugin-sdk` package provides all types, base classes, and testing utilities you need.
   105→
   106→### src/index.ts
   107→
   108→The generated entry point contains every lifecycle hook with inline documentation:
   109→
   110→```typescript
   111→import type { OpenACPPlugin, PluginContext, InstallContext, MigrateContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk'
   112→
   113→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   114→  name: '@myorg/hello-world',
   115→  version: '0.1.0',
   116→  description: 'A greeting plugin for OpenACP',
   117→
   118→  permissions: ['events:read', 'services:register'],
   119→
   120→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext): Promise<void> {
   121→    // Called during server startup. Register services, commands, middleware here.
   122→  },
   123→
   124→  async teardown(): Promise<void> {
   125→    // Called during server shutdown. Clean up resources.
   126→  },
   127→
   128→  async install(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   129→    // Called on `openacp plugin add`. Gather configuration interactively.
   130→  },
   131→
   132→  async configure(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   133→    // Called on `openacp plugin configure`. Update settings.
   134→  },
   135→
   136→  async migrate(ctx: MigrateContext, oldSettings: unknown, oldVersion: string): Promise<unknown> {
   137→    // Called on boot when version changes. Migrate settings.
   138→    return oldSettings
   139→  },
   140→
   141→  async uninstall(ctx: InstallContext, opts: { purge: boolean }): Promise<void> {
   142→    // Called on `openacp plugin remove`. Clean up external resources.
   143→  },
   144→}
   145→
   146→export default plugin
   147→```
   148→
   149→**Lifecycle hooks summary:**
   150→
   151→| Hook | When it runs | Purpose |
   152→|---|---|---|
   153→| `setup(ctx)` | Server startup (dependency order) | Register services, commands, middleware, event listeners |
   154→| `teardown()` | Server shutdown (reverse order) | Clean up timers, connections, resources |
   155→| `install(ctx)` | `openacp plugin add` | Interactive first-time configuration |
   156→| `configure(ctx)` | `openacp plugin configure` | Re-configure settings |
   157→| `migrate(ctx, old, ver)` | Boot, when version changed | Migrate settings between versions |
   158→| `uninstall(ctx, opts)` | `openacp plugin remove` | Clean up external resources |
   159→
   160→---
   161→
   162→## Step 3: Development Workflow
   163→
   164→Install dependencies and build:
   165→
   166→```bash
   167→cd hello-world
   168→npm install
   169→npm run build
   170→```
   171→
   172→### Hot-reload development
   173→
   174→Start OpenACP in dev mode, pointing to your plugin directory:
   175→
   176→```bash
   177→openacp dev .
   178→```
   179→
   180→This will:
   181→1. Compile your TypeScript
   182→2. Start `tsc --watch` in the background
   183→3. Boot OpenACP with your plugin loaded
   184→4. Reload your plugin automatically when files change
   185→
   186→See [Dev Mode](dev-mode.md) for the full guide.
   187→
   188→### Run tests
   189→
   190→```bash
   191→npm test
   192→```
   193→
   194→Tests use Vitest and the `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing` utilities.
   195→
   196→---
   197→
   198→## Step 4: Implement Your Plugin
   199→
   200→Let's turn the template into a greeting plugin that responds to a `/hello` command and logs session events.
   201→
   202→Replace the contents of `src/index.ts`:
   203→
   204→```typescript
   205→import type { OpenACPPlugin, PluginContext, InstallContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk'
   206→
   207→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   208→  name: '@myorg/hello-world',
   209→  version: '0.1.0',
   210→  description: 'A greeting plugin for OpenACP',
   211→
   212→  permissions: ['events:read', 'commands:register'],
   213→
   214→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext): Promise<void> {
   215→    // Register a /hello command
   216→    ctx.registerCommand({
   217→      name: 'hello',
   218→      description: 'Send a greeting',
   219→      usage: '[name]',
   220→      category: 'plugin',
   221→
   222→      async handler(args) {
   223→        const name = args.raw.trim() || 'World'
   224→        return { type: 'text', text: `Hello, ${name}! 👋` }
   225→      },
   226→    })
   227→
   228→    // Listen to session events
   229→    ctx.on('session:created', (event) => {
   230→      ctx.log.info(`New session started: ${event.sessionId}`)
   231→    })
   232→
   233→    ctx.on('session:afterDestroy', (event) => {
   234→      ctx.log.info(`Session ended: ${event.sessionId} (${event.durationMs}ms)`)
   235→    })
   236→
   237→    ctx.log.info('Hello World plugin ready')
   238→  },
   239→
   240→  async teardown(): Promise<void> {
   241→    // Nothing to clean up
   242→  },
   243→
   244→  async install(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   245→    ctx.terminal.log.success('Hello World plugin installed!')
   246→  },
   247→}
   248→
   249→export default plugin
   250→```
   251→
   252→Build and test:
   253→
   254→```bash
   255→npm run build
   256→openacp dev .
   257→```
   258→
   259→Now in your messaging platform, type `/hello` or `/hello Alice` to see the plugin respond.
   260→
   261→---
   262→
   263→## Step 5: Test Your Plugin
   264→
   265→The scaffold includes a basic test. Let's expand it using the SDK testing utilities.
   266→
   267→Replace `src/__tests__/index.test.ts`:
   268→
   269→```typescript
   270→import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
   271→import { createTestContext, createTestInstallContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing'
   272→import plugin from '../index.js'
   273→
   274→describe('@myorg/hello-world', () => {
   275→  it('has correct metadata', () => {
   276→    expect(plugin.name).toBe('@myorg/hello-world')
   277→    expect(plugin.version).toBe('0.1.0')
   278→    expect(plugin.permissions).toContain('commands:register')
   279→  })
   280→
   281→  it('registers the /hello command on setup', async () => {
   282→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   283→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   284→
   285→    expect(ctx.registeredCommands.has('hello')).toBe(true)
   286→    expect(ctx.registeredCommands.get('hello')!.description).toBe('Send a greeting')
   287→  })
   288→
   289→  it('/hello with no args returns default greeting', async () => {
   290→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   291→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   292→
   293→    const response = await ctx.executeCommand('hello', { raw: '' })
   294→    expect(response).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'Hello, World! 👋' })
   295→  })
   296→
   297→  it('/hello with a name returns personalized greeting', async () => {
   298→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   299→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   300→
   301→    const response = await ctx.executeCommand('hello', { raw: 'Alice' })
   302→    expect(response).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'Hello, Alice! 👋' })
   303→  })
   304→
   305→  it('emits log on session events', async () => {
   306→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   307→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   308→
   309→    // Simulate a session:created event
   310→    ctx.emit('session:created', { sessionId: 'test-123' })
   311→    // No error thrown = event handler works
   312→  })
   313→
   314→  it('installs without errors', async () => {
   315→    const ctx = createTestInstallContext({
   316→      pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world',
   317→    })
   318→    await plugin.install!(ctx)
   319→
   320→    // Verify the install function ran
   321→    expect(ctx.terminalCalls).toHaveLength(0) // no prompts needed
   322→  })
   323→
   324→  it('tears down without errors', async () => {
   325→    await expect(plugin.teardown!()).resolves.not.toThrow()
   326→  })
   327→})
   328→```
   329→
   330→Run:
   331→
   332→```bash
   333→npm test
   334→```
   335→
   336→See [Plugin SDK Reference](plugin-sdk-reference.md) for the full testing API including `createTestContext`, `createTestInstallContext`, and `mockServices`.
   337→
   338→---
   339→
   340→## Step 6: Configure and Install
   341→
   342→### Install your plugin locally
   343→
   344→For testing with a real OpenACP instance (not dev mode):
   345→
   346→```bash
   347→# From the plugin directory, build first
   348→npm run build
   349→
   350→# Install from local path
   351→openacp plugin add ./hello-world
   352→```
   353→
   354→### Plugin settings
   355→
   356→If your plugin needs configuration (API keys, preferences), define a `settingsSchema` with Zod and use the `install()` hook:
   357→
   358→```typescript
   359→import { z } from 'zod'
   360→
   361→const settingsSchema = z.object({
   362→  defaultName: z.string().default('World'),
   363→})
   364→
   365→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   366→  // ...
   367→  settingsSchema,
   368→
   369→  async install(ctx: InstallContext) {
   370→    const name = await ctx.terminal.text({
   371→      message: 'Default greeting name:',
   372→      placeholder: 'World',
   373→    })
   374→    await ctx.settings.set('defaultName', name || 'World')
   375→    ctx.terminal.log.success('Configured!')
   376→  },
   377→
   378→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext) {
   379→    const defaultName = ctx.pluginConfig.defaultName ?? 'World'
   380→    // Use defaultName in your command handler...
   381→  },
   382→}
   383→```
   384→
   385→### Enable / disable
   386→
   387→```bash
   388→openacp plugin enable @myorg/hello-world
   389→openacp plugin disable @myorg/hello-world
   390→```
   391→
   392→### Reconfigure
   393→
   394→```bash
   395→openacp plugin configure @myorg/hello-world
   396→```
   397→
   398→---
   399→
   400→## Step 7: Publish
   401→
   402→### Prepare for publishing
   403→
   404→1. Update `version` in both `package.json` and `src/index.ts`
   405→2. Make sure `main` points to `dist/index.js`
   406→3. Ensure `keywords` includes `openacp` and `openacp-plugin`
   407→
   408→### Build and publish
   409→
   410→```bash
   411→npm run build
   412→npm test
   413→npm publish --access public
   414→```
   415→
   416→### How users install your plugin
   417→
   418→```bash
   419→openacp plugin add @myorg/hello-world
   420→```
   421→
   422→This downloads from npm into `~/.openacp/plugins/`, validates the plugin interface, and runs `install()` if defined.
   423→

### Approach 1: Copy + Refactor imports sang SDK (Recommended)

**Ý tưởng:** Copy files sang repo mới nhưng import trực tiếp từ `@openacp/cli` internal paths thay vì qua SDK.

**Nhược điểm:**

- Vẫn cần refactor imports sau khi split

# Extract Discord Plugin to Standalone Package

## Problem

The Discord adapter is bundled as a built-in plugin in OpenACP, meaning `discord.js` and its dependencies are installed for all users even if they don't use Discord. This adds unnecessary weight. The plugin should be a separate package that users install only when needed.

## Solution

Extract `src/plugins/discord/` from the OpenACP monorepo into a standalone package `@open-acp/plugin-discord` in a separate repository. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to export all types/classes the Discord plugin needs. Remove the Discord plugin from the OpenACP repo.

## Target Repository

`/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/` → published as `@open-acp/plugin-discord` on npm.

## Standalone Plugin Structure

```
discord-plugin/
  src/
    index.ts                    # Plugin entry (OpenACPPlugin interface)
    adapter.ts                  # DiscordAdapter (extends MessagingAdapter)
    renderer.ts                 # Discord-specific message rendering
    formatting.ts               # Markdown formatting for Discord
    streaming.ts                # Message streaming/chunking
    draft-manager.ts            # Draft message management
    tool-call-tracker.ts        # Tool call display
```

# Extract Discord Plugin to Standalone Package

## Problem

The Discord adapter is bundled as a built-in plugin in OpenACP, meaning `discord.js` and its dependencies are installed for all users even if they don't use Discord. This adds unnecessary weight. The plugin should be a separate package that users install only when needed.

## Solution

Extract `src/plugins/discord/` from the OpenACP monorepo into a standalone package `@open-acp/plugin-discord` in a separate repository. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to export all types/classes the Discord plugin needs. Remove the Discord plugin from the OpenACP repo.

## Target Repository

`/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/` → published as `@open-acp/plugin-discord` on npm.
